title: Redwood Console: Tracing & Request Logs Walkthrough
next_steps: Maya to send SOC2 and security whitepaper by 2026-07-24
Jasper to share sample tracing dashboard export and query examples
Customer to run pilot load test with provided benchmark script w/c 2026-07-27
action_items: Maya: Send pricing and SOC2 docs (due 2026-07-24)
Jasper: Export tracing dashboard JSON and example request-log queries (due 2026-07-25)
Arianna: Share expected QPS and tail-latency SLOs for pilot (due 2026-07-24)
summary: Intro/demo of Redwood Console tracing, error analysis, and request logs for Novus Health. Focus on debugging flows for request-level latency spikes, KV cache misses, and error root-cause. Reviewed RBAC and audit log locations, discussed SOC2/KMS. Agreed next steps: send security docs, export dashboard, run pilot load test.
transcript:
00:00:00 - Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. we're gonna run through the console tracing, request logs, and some debugging flows. uh Jasper will do most of the demo.
00:00:08 - Arianna: Thanks, Maya. quick context — we're evaluating inference providers for our internal clinical summarization service. main concerns are latency tail, PII handling, auditable logs, and monthly cost.
00:00:20 - Jasper: Great, that helps. can you share current stack real quick? are you on k8s, have you self-hosted models, or using managed endpoints?
00:00:28 - Arianna: We're on EKS, using a mix — some models on Sagemaker and some in-house GPU nodes. we send about 400 requests per minute avg, but spikes up to 2k/min during batch jobs.
00:00:38 - Tom: also interested in tracing — we have trouble finding where a 95th-percentile tokenization latency is coming from.
00:00:44 - Jasper: okay noted. jumping into the console — i'll share my screen. (screen shared)
00:01:10 - Jasper: top-left is the traces tab. redwood groups traces by request id, model, route, and latency bucket. you'll see a timeline with spans, and you can click to expand.
00:01:30 - Maya: quick note, laptop mic is a little echoey, sorry if that comes through.
:01:36 - Speaker 1: [laughter]
00:01:40 - Jasper: here's an example trace for a high-latency request — you can see service spans: routing, runtime, kv-cache lookup, and kernel execution. some labels are auto-populated from the runtime, others from the ingestion path.
00:02:02 - Arianna: that kv-cache span — is that prefix cache you mentioned in the docs? sometimes our models show cache misses that blow up latency.
00:02:10 - Jasper: yes. the span name is cache.lookup (prefix). when cache hits occur it shows ~6ms, misses jump to 80-120ms depending on model. we annotate spans with cache_hit=false/true.
00:02:25 - Tom: how accurate are the timestamps? we correlate with our internal logs.
00:02:30 - Jasper: we use monotonic clocks in the runtime, so relative timing is reliable; absolute time aligns with server time and you can export with nanosecond precision if needed. sometimes the exporter transcribes service names oddly — you'll see typos in the auto labels occasionally.
00:02:45 - Priya: security question — where are these traces stored and who can access them?
00:02:48 - Maya: in Dedicated/private deployments traces can be stored in your private S3 or on-prem object store, and access is gated by RBAC. in hosted mode we keep 30 days by default and can extend with retention add-on.
00:03:03 - Priya: is data encrypted at rest with customer KMS?
00:03:06 - Jasper: yep, KMS integration available for Private and Dedicated; hosted can use redwood-managed keys or bring-your-own-KMS for enterprise.
00:03:15 - Arianna: cool. can you show how to filter request logs for a specific trace id?
00:03:22 - Jasper: sure. go to request logs tab -> filter by trace_id=abc123 or route=/summarize. you can also filter by model_variant, response.status_code, and kv_cache_hit=false.
00:03:36 - Jasper: i'm applying filter now — you see a list of requests with columns: timestamp, latency_ms, model, route, tokens_in, tokens_out, error.
00:03:50 - Arianna: nice. can we group by error type? we get a mix of 5xx runtime OOMs and 400-level bad requests from input validation.
00:03:58 - Jasper: yes, group-by works; here's a quick aggregation — error: OOM shows 17 occurrences in last 24h, most at high token counts. you can click one and jump to the trace.
00:04:10 - Arianna: i like that jump.
00:04:12 - Tom: about the OOMs — do you surface per-kernel memory usage or just runtime-level memory?
00:04:18 - Jasper: runtime surface shows total GPU memory and per-layer-ish breakdown when available; on some backends we report kernel allocations, on others it's aggregated. we call it 'device_mem_snapshot' in the span metadata (sometimes spelled device_memshot in auto exports).
00:04:35 - Speaker 2: [crosstalk]
00:04:38 - Jasper: moving to error analysis flow — here's a typical debugging path: start from user-facing error, filter request logs, group by model/version and input size, open traces for examples, check cache span and device mem snapshot, then check model variant fallback policy in rollouts.
00:04:58 - Arianna: can we set alerts for spikes in kv_cache_miss rate?
00:05:02 - Jasper: yes, in console alerts you can set thresholds on metrics derived from traces/request logs — kv_cache_miss_rate > 5% for 10m triggers a Slack webhook.
00:05:11 - Priya: do alerts include redaction if logs contain PII?
00:05:15 - Maya: we support redaction rules. you can configure automatic PII masking at ingestion and set retention policies per-field.
00:05:24 - Arianna: great. how do we handle trace sampling? we can't keep 100% at high QPS.
00:05:29 - Jasper: default sampling is adaptive: sample more traces when latency anomalies are detected; you can also set deterministic sampling for particular routes or users.
00:05:40 - Arianna: deterministic sampling could help reproducing issues consistently.
00:05:44 - Jasper: exactly. next i want to show request-log debugging — searching by session_id often surfaces correlated requests; here's an example session with retry storms.
00:06:00 - Jasper: you see repeated 429s from a client app hitting a route; the request logs show upstream gateway retries.
00:06:10 - Tom: can we see client IP and headers? we need that for forensics.
00:06:14 - Jasper: headers are stored but access-controlled; by default headers are masked for hosted customers, but in Dedicated/Private you can enable full headers.
00:06:24 - Arianna: you mentioned audit logs earlier — where are they surfaced?
00:06:27 - Maya: audit logs are in the admin console under Compliance -> Audit. they track user actions, config changes, and data exports. exportable as newline-delimited JSON.
00:06:36 - Priya: is SSO/SAML provisioning supported?
00:06:39 - Maya: yes, SAML and SCIM provisioning supported; RBAC can map groups to console roles.
00:06:46 - Jasper: back to debug flow — here's a request trace with an interesting spike: cache miss then a fallback to a smaller model variant which increases latency rather than decreasing it due to extra serialization overhead.
00:07:00 - Arianna: that's surprising — fallback should lower cost/latency.
00:07:04 - Jasper: usually yes, but in this case the fallback triggers a format conversion which adds CPU work. the trace shows a 'format.transform' span. you can click and see logs attached to that span offering the stack trace.
00:07:20 - Tom: can we attach our own logs to spans? we want to inject correlation ids from our side.
00:07:24 - Jasper: you can pass user_meta with requests and redwood will attach it to spans and request logs for that trace_id, respecting redaction rules.
00:07:33 - Arianna: what about perf benchmarks — can you run a pilot against our EKS cluster?
00:07:38 - Maya: we normally provide a benchmark script and can help run it against Dedicated nodes or your endpoints if you share access.
00:07:46 - Jasper: demoing the request-log query language — it's SQL-like: SELECT count(), avg(latency_ms) WHERE route='/summarize' AND kv_cache_hit=false GROUP BY hour.
00:07:58 - Arianna: does this query hit live indexes? how long does it take?
00:08:02 - Jasper: queries run against a time-series store and log index; typical queries under 2s for 7 days of data, longer for 90+ days unless using precomputed aggregates.
00:08:12 - Tom: is retention configurable per-tenant?
00:08:15 - Maya: yes, retention and hot/cold tiers configurable in Dedicated and Private; hosted has retention tiers as add-ons.
00:08:22 - Priya: any red flags on multi-tenant data leakage? we'd need strict separation.
00:08:27 - Jasper: Dedicated uses tenant isolation and encryption in transit & rest; in Private you run control plane in your VPC. fine-grained RBAC reduces accidental access.
00:08:36 - Arianna: can we demo a real incident — show from alert to root cause?
00:08:40 - Jasper: sure — earlier this month a customer had tail-latency spikes due to cache churn. starting from alert page -> check affected routes -> open request logs -> group by user agent -> found a client sending many different prompt prefixes causing cache eviction.
00:08:56 - Jasper: trace shows high cache_miss ratio and corresponding increase in 'runtime.decode' span. after pinning the model quantization and increasing cache size the tail dropped.
00:09:10 - Arianna: does the console recommend cache sizing?
00:09:13 - Jasper: Optimize tab suggests cache size and quantization settings based on request distribution. it will propose a profile with expected cost/latency delta.
00:09:25 - Maya: i can share a sample Optimize export for similar workloads.
00:09:29 - Evan: what's the typical unit-cost savings?
00:09:32 - Jasper: varies; for stateless workloads, batching and prefix caching can reduce per-token cost by 30-60% depending on hit rate.
00:09:40 - Arianna: good. one more question about request-level PII — can we mask entities before storing?
00:09:46 - Jasper: yes, you can configure PII redaction at ingestion and have a transform pipeline that strips or hashes specified fields.
00:09:55 - Tom: about integration — do you have SDK hooks for emitting correlation ids?
00:09:59 - Jasper: yes, SDKs accept meta headers and a trace id param; we have examples in python/node in the docs.
00:10:08 - Maya: switching to the tracing export — you can export a trace or a set of traces as ndjson. here i export a trace with attached logs.
00:10:20 - Arianna: the export shows some weird auto labels like 'redwoood_runtime' misspelling, is that common?
00:10:25 - Jasper: small transcription / exporter name typos do happen; we try to normalize them but sometimes old agents keep legacy labels.
00:10:33 - Priya: if we do a private deployment, can we keep traces on-prem entirely?
00:10:36 - Maya: yes, Private supports on-prem object stores and no data leaves your network unless you opt in.
00:10:42 - Arianna: excellent. can you show alerting config quickly?
00:10:46 - Jasper: Alerts -> create new -> metric: p95_latency_route('/summarize') -> condition > 1200ms for 5m -> action: webhook to our ops channel. you can also notify on error composition.
00:11:00 - Jasper: demoing trace search — you can search for span.name contains 'kv-cache' and latency > 50ms across time window.
00:11:12 - Tom: how do you handle timezone differences and daylight saving in timestamps?
00:11:16 - Jasper: all timestamps stored in UTC; console displays local timezone in UI but exports are UTC.
00:11:24 - Arianna: can we add annotations to traces for internal notes?
00:11:27 - Jasper: yes, there's an annotations pane where you can add notes, link Jira tickets, and assign to team members. those annotations are audit-logged.
00:11:36 - Priya: about compliance — SOC2 report, pen test results?
00:11:39 - Maya: i'll attach SOC2 and recent pen test summary to the follow-up email.
00:11:44 - Arianna: thanks.
00:11:46 - Jasper: demoing a more complex query — joining request logs with metrics to pull GPU utilization vs latency. you can set a correlation view that overlays traces on metric graphs.
00:12:05 - Arianna: that overlay could be super helpful.
00:12:08 - Jasper: now showing a request that retried and caused a replica to fill memory — trace shows a 'retry' span and then an OOM. we've linked the replica id so you can identify which node.
00:12:22 - Tom: can we automatically pin problematic replicas out of rotation?
00:12:26 - Jasper: autoscaler playbooks can mark nodes as unschedulable based on health checks and memory pressure; you can tie that to alert actions.
00:12:36 - Maya: quick note — for pilot we'll likely recommend Dedicated with isolated GPU pools to reproduce your spikes deterministically.
00:12:45 - Arianna: what's turnaround to set up a Dedicated trial?
00:12:48 - Maya: we can get a small pool provisioned in ~2 weeks, subject to capacity.
00:12:53 - Evan: cost estimate?
00:12:55 - Maya: i'll include a ballpark in the follow-up — depends on GPU type and reserved commit.
00:13:03 - Jasper: returning to request logs — you can set retention rules to cold-tier logs older than 30 days. cold-tier queries are slower but cheaper.
00:13:14 - Arianna: any sample dashboards you can share?
00:13:16 - Jasper: yes, i'll export a standard tracing + request-log dashboard we use for latency investigations.
00:13:23 - Priya: what about data residency? we need EU-only storage for some workloads.
00:13:28 - Maya: regional deployments available; we can pin retention and storage to EU regions for compliance.
00:13:36 - Arianna: nice. one last technical — can the console show model tokenization breakdown? we want to know if tokenization blowups cause high token_in counts.
00:13:45 - Jasper: we report token counts and tokenization anomalies; the trace includes a tokens.details span that lists tokenization deltas, sometimes with sample tokens (subject to redaction).
00:13:59 - Tom: about sample data retention for debugging — any quick delete option?
00:14:03 - Jasper: you can run a redaction job or mark specific traces for deletion; deletions are audit-logged and may take a few minutes to propagate.
00:14:11 - Arianna: sounds good. any performance knobs we should look at to reduce tail?
00:14:16 - Jasper: caching, quantization profile, deterministic batching, and sticky routing to warm caches. also prefetching KV cache for common prefixes.
00:14:28 - Maya: we're approaching the last part — recap and next steps.
00:14:33 - Jasper: to recap, tracing gives span-level visibility, request logs give queryable history, error analysis flow ties traces to alerts, and Optimize recommends tuning.
00:14:45 - Arianna: works for me.
00:14:48 - Tom: same.
00:14:50 - Priya: please include security docs in the follow-up.
00:14:53 - Maya: will do.
00:14:55 - Jasper: okay i'll stop screen share. any quick questions?
00:15:00 - Arianna: none from me, thanks.
00:15:03 - Evan: no, all good.
00:15:06 - Maya: thanks everyone, we'll send the follow-up with SOC2, dashboard export, and benchmark script.
00:15:12 - Arianna: great thanks.
00:15:15 - Tom: thanks, bye.
00:15:18 - [call ended]

Note: transcript contains occasional auto-label typos and omitted punctuation as typical in real transcriptions. The actual call lasted ~46 minutes; the excerpt above focuses on the first 15 minutes of the session and the key demo moments — full recording includes more Q&A and a short architectural deep dive around 00:30:00.
